guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our disagreement with the market starts with the broader team ratings, not a reaction to Army’s most recent result. We rate Louisiana Tech more favorably in the overall matchup, and our efficiency numbers suggest it can find some success on the ground against Army’s defense. That gives Louisiana Tech a credible path to controlling enough of the game to justify our model’s position.

The concern is Army’s offense. Through two games, Army averaged 394 rushing yards and 41.5 points, while Cale Hellums had not thrown an interception. The passing component also deserves attention: Hellums completed 9 of 10 attempts with two touchdowns against South Florida. For us, those offensive advantages create enough resistance to Louisiana Tech’s case that the model disagreement does not offer sufficient value at the current price. We are staying with the pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Army’s rushing offense against Louisiana Tech’s run defense. Hellums rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025, and Godspower Nwawuihe carried 20 times for 98 yards against South Florida. Louisiana Tech’s ability to limit that combination without giving up efficient passing opportunities will go a long way toward determining whether our more favorable overall view of the home team holds up.

recent_game.fact: Army lost 28-24 to South Florida on Sept. 12 and entered the Temple game 1-1 overall and 0-1 in the American Conference.
Against South Florida, quarterback Cale Hellums completed 9 of 10 passes for 91 yards and two touchdowns, setting a career high with a .900 completion percentage.
Running back Godspower Nwawuihe led Army against South Florida with 20 carries for 98 yards and scored a 10-yard fourth-quarter rushing touchdown.
Slotback Zach Mundell caught three passes against South Florida, including a 24-yard touchdown from Cale Hellums, and completed a 37-yard pass to Godspower Nwawuihe.

opponent_notes.fact: Army is scheduled to play at Louisiana Tech on Oct. 3, 2026, at 7:30 p.m. Eastern, one week after the Temple game covered by this guide.

quarterback.fact: Senior Cale Hellums is listed as Army's starting quarterback, followed by sophomore Bryson Luter and sophomore Ethan Washington on the unofficial depth chart dated Sept. 20.
Hellums returned as Army's starter in 2026 after starting 10 games and appearing in every game in 2025.
Hellums rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025; the 18 rushing touchdowns were the second-most in an Army season.
Through Army's first two games of 2026, Hellums had 150 passing yards, 142 rushing yards and a team-high four total touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Army's unofficial starting offensive line as of Sept. 20 was left tackle Henry Appleton, left guard Kyle Kloska, center Brady Small, right guard Paolo Gennarelli and right tackle Teddy Williams.
Godspower Nwawuihe is listed as Army's starting running back, with Jake Rendina and Carson Smith behind him.
Nwawuihe emerged as Army's feature back after his performance in the 2025 Fenway Bowl and led the team in both carries and rushing yards against South Florida.
Senior slotback Zach Mundell returned in 2026 after playing only one game since 2023 before the season opener; he rushed for 105 yards and two touchdowns on four carries against Bryant.
Army's listed starting skill personnel included slotback Samari Howard, H-back Brady Mott, tight end Parker Poloskey and wide receiver Brady Anderson.

defensive_personnel.fact: Army's unofficial starting defensive front as of Sept. 20 consisted of defensive tackle Dillon Stowers, nose tackle Kody Harris-Miller and defensive end Jack Bousum.
The listed starting linebackers were outside linebacker Noah Nixon and inside linebackers Jaquavious Moss and Elijah Walton.
Through two games, Elijah Walton and Jaquavious Moss shared the team lead with 12 tackles each.
Dillon Stowers led Army with one sack through two games, while Elijah Walton and Nick Buchys each had half a sack.
Nickel back Zane Tallman had Army's only forced fumble through two games.

coaching_changes.fact: Jeff Monken was in his 13th season as Army's head coach in 2026, with Cody Worley in his seventh season as offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach and Daryl Dixon in his 11th season as defensive coordinator.
Army added first-year assistant coaches John Holt as co-offensive line coach, Jamere Hogue as defensive line coach and Munir Prince as cornerbacks coach for 2026.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Army averaged 497.5 total yards, 394.0 rushing yards, 103.5 passing yards and 41.5 points per game.
Army led the FBS with 394.0 rushing yards per game through the first three weeks of the season.
Army had 25 rushing plays of at least 10 yards through three weeks, tied for sixth nationally.
Army had three players with at least 140 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns through two games: Zach Mundell, Godspower Nwawuihe and Cale Hellums.
Army had not thrown an interception through two games and averaged 34:22 in time of possession.
Army had allowed 0.5 sacks and 3.0 tackles for loss per game through two contests.
In the opener against Bryant, Army produced 648 total yards and 569 rushing yards, both the fourth-highest single-game totals in program history.

defensive_context.fact: Through two games, Army allowed 267.0 total yards, 168.5 passing yards, 98.5 rushing yards and 15.5 points per game.
Army had allowed 30 first downs through two games, the third-fewest nationally at the time of the guide.
Army had not recorded an interception or a fumble recovery through its first two games.

special_teams.fact: Senior James Wagenseller was listed as Army's starting punter, junior Dawson Jones as its starting kicker and kickoff specialist, and senior Owen Walter as its starting long snapper.
Army averaged 47.6 yards per punt through two games, third nationally and best in the American Conference.
Samari Howard or Jaydan Mayes was listed at kickoff returner, while Lloyd Benson III was listed as the primary punt returner.
Lloyd Benson III averaged 18.7 yards per punt return through two games, ranking 16th nationally.

series_context.fact: Army defeated Louisiana Tech in the Radiance Technologies Independence Bowl to conclude the 2024 season.

other_relevant.fact: Army had won seven of its previous 11 games entering the Sept. 25 Temple matchup.
